releases.displayName: Space Engineers: Warfare 3 Update & Pack Live Now!

items.text: Hello, Engineers!

Warfare 3 is here, bringing one of the biggest combat overhauls Space Engineers has ever seen. From Combat NPCs, guided missiles and torpedoes to countermeasure flares, EMP weapons, Jump Detection, new automation options, and much more, this update changes how battles are fought, defended, and engineered.
Everything in this update is free. Alongside it, we're releasing the Warfare 3 Pack with new decorative blocks and variants to expand your creative options.
If you own Space Engineers, everything below is yours - no extra purchase needed.

Warfare 3 makes combat more dynamic for both PvE and PvP players. Guided weapons, countermeasures, EMP technology, new targeting tools, expanded automation and configurable world settings create new decisions before, during and after every engagement - and give Engineers more ways to design ships, defenses and weapons around the battles they expect to face.
Combat NPCs are one of the most important achievements in Warfare 3 - and the result of work we have been building up across several previous updates.

Economy 2 laid the groundwork for interactable NPCs, and we have been expanding their role ever since. Warfare 3 is where that work really comes together: NPCs can now appear across all encounter types, from passing Cargo Ships to the most dangerous Factorum locations.

Until now, many encounters could feel like you had arrived after everyone had already left. That starts to change. Hostile NPCs patrol their grids and fight back when you attack, turning boarding and salvage into a much more dangerous job. Other NPCs bring movement, chatter, and a sense that these places actually belong to someone.

Their messages can also give you clues about who they are, what is happening, and why that ship or station is there in the first place. It is a small change on paper, but it makes encounters feel far less like empty structures and much more like places with people, stories, and something worth defending.

We are especially excited to see what this does to Factorum Encounters. They were already among the most dangerous places in Space Engineers. Now, getting inside, taking control, and escaping with the rewards will come with an entirely new kind of resistance.
This is a major step toward making the Space Engineers universe feel more alive, and we cannot wait to see how its new inhabitants change the way you explore, board, fight, and survive.

Warfare 3 introduces guided weapons for both large and small grids. The new Torpedo Launcher fires several torpedo variants, including standard, Light, Heavy and Armor Piercing Torpedoes, while the new Homing Missile gives existing rocket launchers a guided ammunition option.

Guided projectiles use target lock and predictive guidance to pursue moving grids. Supported static weapons can also target specific subsystems, allowing Engineers to aim their guided munitions at critical systems such as weapons, propulsion or power.
[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
Torpedo Launcher (1 block, S grid + 1 block, L grid) - Launch a range of guided torpedoes, from fast-seeking variants to heavy anti-armor payloads, and adapt your firepower to the target.

The Firework Launcher has been renamed to the Flare Launcher and can now fire countermeasure flares capable of disrupting seeking missiles and torpedoes. Their effectiveness depends on the incoming munition, the distance between the missile and the flares, and the strength of the deployed flare coverage.
Flares are highly effective against lighter guided weapons, while heavier torpedoes are more resistant and may need to be destroyed by point-defense systems.
Gatling Turret accuracy has also been increased by 25%, making the turrets more effective in this role.

The Prototech Microwave Emitter introduces EMP warfare to Space Engineers. This warhead-like block charges before releasing a disruptive microwave pulse that temporarily disables affected grids and exposes nearby characters to radiation.

After discharging, the emitter damages itself and must be repaired before it can be used again. Fully powered-down grids can avoid the EMP shutdown, creating opportunities for carefully timed defensive power-downs, surprise attacks, mines and custom EMP torpedoes.

Weapons that support multiple ammunition types now allow you to choose the desired ammunition directly from their controls or cycle through available options using toolbar actions.
The new Force Reload action lets you unload the currently loaded ammunition and immediately switch to another selected type, giving you more control over your weapons during combat.
Assault and Artillery Shells now deal area-of-effect damage around their point of impact.

Warfare 3 also introduces a wide range of combat improvements:
Hand Weapon Target Locking - The PRO-1 Rocket Launcher can now lock onto grids, display a lead indicator and fire Homing Missiles at locked targets.
Relative Dampening on Hostile Grids - A new world setting controls whether players can use Relative Dampeners to match the movement of hostile grids.
Jump Detection - Heavy grids performing long-distance jumps can generate temporary Jump Signature GPS markers, creating new opportunities for pursuit and interception.
Incoming Missile Event - Event Controllers can detect incoming guided missiles and torpedoes, allowing automated alarms, defensive systems or countermeasure launches.
Targeting Improvements - Target lock now uses the center of a grid rather than its Pivot Point, while the Target Info LCD App provides more useful subsystem information.

Anti-Personnel Turret Rework - The Interior Turret has been renamed to the Anti-Personnel Turret and now uses its own dedicated ammunition. The damage was rebalanced, and we disabled Anti-Personnel Turret’s ability to do headshots.
More Consistent Explosions - Stored items, floating items and temporary cargo now use unified explosion calculations, making player-made "nukes" more predictable.

Camera and Turret Improvements - Cameras can now pan and rotate their view, while turret view rotation can be adjusted for upside-down and side-mounted installations. We also added a new camera overlay.
Reduced Weapon block PCUs - Thanks to our game optimizations, many weapons are receiving PCU reductions!
Turret Idle Rotation is now disabled by default.

Rocket Turrets Missile Targeting - Missile turrets now gained the option to target incoming hostile missiles & torpedoes to provide additional protection that is especially effective for static defences.

The universe is changing - and the encounters scattered across it are changing with it. Existing encounters have been refreshed with new weapons, including the Prototech Microwave Emitter appearing in selected Factorum fights.
The Factorum have been busy too. A brand-new encounter featuring the Prototech Microwave Emitter brings another dangerous challenge to discover, assault, and survive.
This block has huge potential for both combat and non-combat applications.

Separation Charge can destroy itself on command, with a controlled explosion that doesn’t damage anything it’s touching, but before it destroys itself, it fires a series of actions. So whatever you set up will be triggered, then it will destroy itself. It’s great for breakaway torpedoes, and lets you build these types of setups without the need for a subgrid like a hinge or a rotor - and it uses a fraction of the PCU, while still allowing fuel and items to pass through its conveyor.

The really powerful part is the action sequence, which will make this such a cool block for so many applications. It could be a missile, a mine, splitting a grid off a projector, multi-stage rocket systems - I think our players will really surprise us with what they create - and I can’t wait to see it.
[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]

Separation Charge (1 block, S grid + 1 block, L grid) - Detach sections of your grid on command while triggering assigned actions - ideal for torpedoes, mines, staged systems, and other engineered creations.

Jump Detection is a new optional world setting that can reveal where large, heavy grids emerge after using a Jump Drive. The heavier the grid and the farther it travels, the stronger its jump signature becomes - allowing nearby players to pick up a temporary GPS marker at its destination.

This opens up new opportunities to hunt down and intercept other players. The feature can be disabled in the world settings, and its thresholds and values are easily accessible and customizable through modding.

We're also introducing a new world setting for Artificial Mass blocks and Space Balls. These blocks are commonly used to build "Gravity Drives," which are incredibly fun but can be performance intensive and difficult to balance in PvP.
We know many players enjoy these creations, so rather than imposing restrictions on everyone, we're giving communities the option to disable these blocks if they choose.

These blocks are also gaining a new function! They now act as gravity anchors on planets and moons, adding mass when enabled on planetary surfaces. This opens up new possibilities, from improving vehicle handling in low gravity to creating mechanisms that shift their mass on demand… Did someone say trebuchet?

Colorful Icons have been at the top of the feedback tickets on our support site for a long time. It’s a big task - and one we couldn’t do without dedicating a fair amount of resources to it. Our game has over 1,700 items that use icons - from blocks and components to tools and consumables... It’s a lot to adjust, and we wanted to do it right.

Alongside what we wanted for the base game, one of our biggest goals was to give our modding community a tool they could use to match the lighting, composition, and overall style of our new icons. We wanted to give them the ability to update their mods quickly and with as little hassle as possible, helping their creations stay visually consistent with the vanilla game. The Icon Studio is now available inside our ModSDK - I’m very happy with what’s come out of this endeavor, and I can’t wait to see some of our favorite community additions updated in full color.

notes.title: Separated Toolbar Actions & Additional Set Value Actions

items.text: Automation is getting more precise. Many existing toggle actions now have separate On and Off controls, giving you more predictable behavior when building complex systems with cockpits, wheel suspensions, AI blocks, landing gear, antennas, and more.

We are also expanding Set Value actions across several blocks, letting you directly define values such as Event Controller thresholds, light settings, wheel properties, Gravity Generator acceleration, and Timer Block delays. This gives Engineers finer control over automated systems without relying on repeated toggles or incremental adjustments.
[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]

Longer Conveyor Pipes (1 block, S grid + 3 blocks, L grid) - The standard Conveyor Tube, Reinforced Conveyor Tube, and Heavy Industry DLC Conveyor Pipes are all receiving additional variants that are 3 times longer.
Round Flat Atmospheric Thruster Set (2 blocks, S grid + 2 blocks, L grid) - A sleek, rounded take on the Flat Atmospheric Thruster, giving you more options for clean, compact atmospheric builds.

Guided weapons gained additional configurable modding fields, giving modders much deeper control over how missiles and torpedoes behave. Seeking can be tuned through values such as guidance range, predictive guidance, lock-on and lock-maintain cones, turn rate, and launch requirements, while projectile lifetime can now be defined independently of maximum trajectory. Splash-damage values are also exposed for supported ammunition, opening the door to much more varied custom weapons - from agile interceptors to slow, heavy torpedoes and specialized area-effect munitions.

Modders can also define how resistant individual guided munitions are to countermeasure flares, as well as whether specific projectile types can be targeted by missile-defense systems. Together, these options make it possible to create much more distinct weapon roles, counterplay, and defensive interactions.
Modders are getting new tools too. Warfare 3 introduces new Screen Space and Drawing ModAPIs that open up a much wider range of possibilities for custom interfaces and on-screen information.

Mods can now draw text and sprites directly in screen space, create entirely new UI screens, and generate textures dynamically. That means modders are no longer limited to adapting existing interface elements - they can build purpose-made displays and visual systems around the needs of their mods.

These APIs can support everything from custom HUD elements and status readouts to dedicated control interfaces, visual indicators, and much more elaborate in-game tools. More importantly, they give creators a foundation to experiment with interface ideas that simply were not possible before.
And rather than just tell you what these tools can do, we asked Space Engineers modders to show us. Here are some of the amazing new possibilities they have already been exploring:
…and more! There are many additional improvements and fixes in the Warfare 3 Update - you can explore everything included in the detailed Changelog.

We have big plans for 2027! As Space Engineers enters its 14th year of development, we're proud of how far it's come, but we know some parts are showing their age. We hear you, and we're putting your feedback to work! We're ready to tackle long standing pain points and modernize the parts of the game that need it most. Expect more frequent updates and more communication from our team as we make Space Engineers even better.

We're not stopping at improvements! We've never shied away from a challenge. Space Engineers has grown from a simple sandbox into a populated world with fully destructible planets, and we're far from finished! We have some major gameplay additions planned, and we're ready to take Space Engineers into an exciting new era. Stay tuned! We'll be back with more very, very soon!
NPC Combat
NPC characters can now spawn on all encounter types. Existing encounters have been updated with chances to spawn NPCs, if appropriate for their individual story.
NPCs can send chat messages, adding more story information to their individual encounters.
NPCs can move around grids and defend the grid when attacked.
Combat Systems Overhaul
Guided Missiles and Torpedoes
Added Homing Missiles as a possible ammo type for rocket launchers
Added Torpedo Launcher block and multiple torpedo variants.
Target lock is used for predictive guidance on projectiles.
Added subsystem target support for static weapons that support guided munitions.
Modding: Added numerous configurable fields for seeking weapons, as well as support for projectile lifetime and splash damage values.
EMP Weaponry
Added Prototech Microwave Emitter, a warhead-like block which temporarily disables all grids in the area and exposes characters to radiation.
Countermeasure Flares
Firework Launcher has been renamed to Flare Launcher
Flares can be fired to disrupt seeking missiles and torpedoes.
Countermeasure effectiveness varies based on the missile type, flare coverage, and how close the flares are to the missile.
Hand Weapon Target Locking
Added target locking and lead indicator to PRO-1 Rocket Launcher. This weapon now fires Homing Missiles, instead of dumbfire Rockets.
Ammunition Switching
For blocks that accept multiple ammunition types, you can select the desired type directly from weapon controls or cycle the selection with toolbar actions.
Added Force Reload action for weapons, allowing for loaded ammo to be swapped with a different type.
Jump Detection
This new PvP world setting makes heavy ships performing long-distance jumps generate a temporary Jump Signature GPS visible to nearby players, creating new opportunities for interception and pursuit.
Relative Dampening on Hostile Grids
This new world setting controls whether players can use Relative Dampeners on hostile grids.
Artificial Mass Block Changes

Added “Enable Gravity Drives” world setting. Gravity Drives are now disabled by default and can be enabled in world settings if desired. Mass blocks will only respect artificial gravity if this setting is enabled.
Artificial Mass now interacts with natural gravity, allowing lighter weight craft (such as rovers) to be better anchored to gravity.
New Event Controller Event
Incoming Missile: Allows players to set up automated defense responses when a guided missile or torpedo is incoming.
Colorful Icons
Added new full-color renders for all blocks and items.
Enabled AOE damage on Assault and Artillery Shells
Interior Turret Rework
Renamed Interior Turret to Anti-Personnel Turret
Added a new dedicated ammo box for the Anti-Personnel Turret
The damage was rebalanced and we disabled Anti-Personnel Turret’s ability to do headshots
Adjusted Explosive Values of Items
Items stored in cargo, floating object items, and items stored in temporary containers now have unified explosion formulas. This makes all “nuke” explosions caused by large stockpiles consistent.
Adjusted how explosive items are, with the Explosive component being the most explosive.
Targeting Info App changes
Target Info LCD App now shows more relevant target information, allowing combatants to better identify subsystem targets.
Target Lock Improvements
Target lock now displays the distance to locked target based on the center of the grid’s bounding box, instead of using the grid’s Pivot Point. This should result in much more accurate numbers.
Increased accuracy of Gatling Turrets 25% to serve better as point defense
Camera Improvements
Added the ability to pan the camera when viewing through a camera block.
Added the ability to rotate the view angle of a camera block, as well as on turret blocks.
Added a new camera overlay.
Turret Block Improvements
Turret Idle Rotation has been disabled by default.
Added the ability to rotate the view angle of a turret while manually controlling the weapon.
Missile turrets now gained the option to target incoming hostile missiles & torpedoes to provide additional protection that is especially effective for static defences.

We revisited the hit box size of every turret with the main goal to scale them down a little bit and make them more accurate to the physical model. This has the effect of slightly better survivability of turrets as they get hit less.

releases.displayName: Space Engineers: Prosperity Update & Pack Live Now!

items.text: Hello, Engineers!

The Prosperity Update makes Space Engineers feel more alive, useful, and rewarding: better economy services, safer grid recovery, and more ways to build the kind of base, station, or ship that feels great.

Explore a new Factorum encounter and hunt down the new Prototech O2/H2 Generator, track missing ships with the new Ping Grid button, and enjoy improvements to Projector, Contracts, the Services Terminal and economy systems.
We’ve also added a small grid Flat Collector - a handy new block for all the farmers among you.
Full Blog Post
Support Portal
Everything in this update is free. Alongside it, we're releasing the Prosperity Pack with new decorative blocks and variants to expand your creative options.
If you own Space Engineers, everything below is yours - no extra purchase needed.

Apparently, the Factorum have not shown us everything they have been hiding. New rumors are spreading through the void: strange signals and valuable Prototech waiting for any engineer bold enough to go after it. Of course, that means some of you are already plotting the fastest way in - and the most explosive way out.

A new Factorum Global Encounter has been added into your worlds. Track it down, break through their defenses, and see what secrets you can bring back in one piece. As always, getting your hands on it will not be as simple as grinding down a few blocks and flying home.
Economy 2 added new ways to store, repair, recover, and salvage grids. With this update, we focused on making those systems clearer, safer, and more predictable in normal gameplay.

Services Terminals now give you better feedback about what is happening with your stored grids. If a grid cannot be stored or deployed yet, the terminal should do a better job explaining why - for example, if the grid is moving, recently damaged, or otherwise not ready. This should make grid storage feel less like a black box and more like a proper station service.

We’ve also improved how grid retrieval works. Server owners can now control whether stored grids can be pulled from very distant locations, and retrieval timing can take distance into account. For players, this means Economy 2 servers can be tuned for different playstyles - from convenient ship storage to more grounded logistics where location matters.

Precision deployment is getting a useful improvement too. You can now set the Precision Mode marker to your current character position, making it much easier to bring a stored grid back exactly where you need it. Less guessing, less nudging, fewer “almost perfect” deployments.

Repair, salvage, and storage rules have also been tightened up. Grids with hostile blocks attached are now handled more carefully, helping prevent cases where players could bypass hacking or ownership rules through station services. Modders and scenario creators also get more flexibility, including new options for enabling repair and salvage services on player-made grids.

Player stores also have a new option to opt out of Item Search. This gives shop owners more control over how their listings appear, especially if they want to run a more private store, keep certain offers local, or avoid cluttering global search results. Your store can still exist and function normally - it just does not have to advertise every listing to everyone through Item Search.
We’ve also improved some of the wording around Store Blocks and Market Search, making listings and search behavior easier to understand.
Overall, these changes should make Economy 2 feel more reliable in day-to-day play - whether you are storing a hauler, recovering a damaged ship, running a server, or building a custom scenario.

We’ve cleaned up several projector controls and UI behaviors. Movement and rotation directions should feel more consistent, sliders should behave more predictably, and projector settings that were previously locked at various stages can now be manipulated at any time.. The goal is simple: less fighting the interface, more building the grid you actually wanted to build - especially when working with complex blueprints or finishing repairs after a rough encounter.
Lost your ship again? It happens. Space is big, GPS management is a lifestyle, and sometimes your favorite grid ends up somewhere you definitely meant to remember.

The new Ping Grid button helps with that. From the Info screen, you can now generate a GPS point for one of your grids, making it much easier to track down ships, rovers, stations, and other creations you may have misplaced during your adventures.

The GPS point marks the grid’s current location and stays available until you remove it, so you can find your way back later. It’s a simple improvement, but for anyone who has ever lost a mining ship, scout rover, or “temporary” construction platform - this one should save some headaches.

The Space Respawn Ship has been modernized and rebuilt with survival in mind. Important systems are easier to see at a glance, so new and returning engineers can better understand what the ship has, what it needs, and how to keep it flying. It should serve as a better starting point - giving you exactly what you need to start your adventure out in the void.
[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
Prototech O2/H2 Generator (1 block, L grid) - The latest Factorum innovation is here! Refill fuel and oxygen up to 10x faster, using less power than a standard generator.
Flat Collector (1 block, S grid) - Slim, sleek, and easy to fit into compact builds. Harvest crops like a pro with this space-saving collector!
Structural Platform Conveyor (1 block, L grid) - You asked, and we heard you! Hide conveyor lines inside your Structural Platform foundations for cleaner, smarter ship and station layouts.
Short Stairs (1 block, L grid) - Small space? No problem. These airtight stairs keep compact builds walkable, connected, and pressurized.
Passage 2 Frame (1 block, L grid) - A sleek, space-saving extension of the Passage 2 block. Use it to polish your interiors, create compact access points, or frame machinery and thrusters with style.

There are many additional improvements and fixes in the Prosperity Update - you can explore everything included in the detailed Changelog.
Our next Space Engineers update, Warfare 3, is shaping up to be a big one! We aim to deliver it to you in November/December 2026.

Expect new weapon types, new combat systems, and changes designed to make battles, PvP, and ship-to-ship engagements more dynamic. This time, your weapons may not be aimed only at other players... There are new threats on the horizon.
We are always looking for ways to improve, and that includes adding value to prior releases. During this update, we are adding new content to Decorative Pack #2.
Those who already own Decorative Pack 2 will get this content for free, as part of the update.

The Prosperity Pack adds over 50 new blocks - Sloped Cockpits, Bulky Hydrogen Tanks, Steep and Solid Stairs, Battery Banks, Square Railings, Decorative Server Racks, Cable Runs, Round and Square Lights. These are cosmetic and decorative blocks that don't affect gameplay balance.
If you enjoy Space Engineers and want to support its continued development, this is a great way to do it - and you'll get a lot of new building options in return.

Square Railings (13 blocks, L grid) - A sturdy safety railing with a solid frame, perfect for adding structure, protection, and visual variety to walkways and platforms.

Cable Run (7 blocks, L grid) - Thick industrial frames packed with large cables, perfect for exposed parts or technical detail to corridors, machinery rooms, and workspaces.

Round & Square Lights (2 blocks, L grid + 2 block, S grid) - Round and Square light fixtures with large, visible emitters. Perfect for illuminating interiors, adding strong visible light sources to runways or landing pads, and keeping your builds bright.

items.text: Hello, Engineers!

The Economy 2 Update is here - and it changes how you play. Store entire grids and redeploy them when you need them. Repair your ship at a trade station without replacing a single component. Hunt bounties, haul cargo through pirate space, and sell scrap for credits. Trade stations now have NPCs walking around inside them. And further ModAPI improvements open new possibilities for modders, server gamemasters, and scenario makers.
Full Blog Post
Services Terminal Guide
Support Portal
Everything in this update is free. Alongside it, we're releasing the Economy 2 Pack with new decorative blocks and variants to expand your creative options.
We’re bringing you all the important gameplay changes for free in our Core Systems Update.

notes.title: Services Terminal: Grid Storage, Repair & Salvage

items.text: The Services Terminal block is one of the core new infrastructure features of the Economy 2 Update. Its purpose is to give players new ways to quickly store, repair, and sell grids. Repair and Salvage services are exclusive to the economy system, making trade stations useful hubs of activity, and not just of an optional side system.
[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
Services Terminal (1 block, L grid)
Grid Storage

The Services Terminal lets you store entire grids and bring them back when you need them. Free up your PCU and unleash your creativity, store a specialized grid until an activity calls for its use, or clean up the crowded area around your busy base.

When retrieving a stored grid, you can deploy it into the general area or place it more precisely by using Precision Mode controls. These controls give you better control over where your ship appears and makes it easier to handle tighter parking spaces or more organized hangars.

Grid Storage can also be used in more flexible ways depending on how the terminal is set up. An "Anyone Can Use" option allows other players to interact with the storage system at trade stations or allied bases, and a per-grid "Share with Faction" option lets you share specific stored grids with your faction members.

By default, retrieving a grid can take some time, but new world settings can let you dial in these times to make it behave exactly how you want.When retrieval timers are enabled, you can expedite the redeployment process by paying Space Credits. This block is loaded with optional settings, allowing admins the ability to configure to their liking - including whether or not items are allowed to remain inside stored grids, giving server owners and scenario creators fine control over how the system can be used.
Grid Repair

The Grid Repair Service lets you bring a damaged grid to an NPC Trade Station and pay Space Credits to quickly restore damaged systems. It is a fast and convenient way to get ships and vehicles back into working shape without handling every missing component and damaged block manually - making it a practical recovery option after combat, accidents, or long expeditions. To use this service, you must be the majority owner of the grid.
Grid Salvage

Grid Salvage lets you bring a grid to an NPC Trade Station and sell it as scrap for Space Credits through the Services Terminal. It is a quick and convenient way to turn damaged, outdated, or unwanted ships and vehicles into useful credits instead of taking them apart by hand. To use this service, you must be the majority owner of the grid. If the grid still contains items, you will get a warning before completing the sale, as those items will not be recoverable after the transaction is complete.

The Economy 2 Update brings a major overhaul to the economy systems in Space Engineers, making trading, station visits, and market information much easier to understand and use. With the new Economy Overview, Item Search, Store Block improvements, and expanded modding support, economy gameplay now feels more connected, more readable, and more responsive to player activity.
Economy Overview

The old Contracts screen has been repurposed into the new Economy Overview, giving you a better view of important store and contract information in one place. It is designed to make price changes, item availability, and the overall state of the economy much easier to interact with while playing.

When interacting with NPC-owned Store Blocks and Contract Blocks, you can now also see the time remaining until the next economy update, making it easier to understand when stores will restock and when new contracts will become available. The default time between Store Block restocks and Contract Block refreshes has also been reduced, helping the economy feel more active and responsive. This timing can also be configured on Dedicated Servers.
Item Search

A new Item Search tab has been added to Store Blocks and the Economy Overview, making it much easier to find the items you need. You can remotely search listings from NPC and player-built stores, compare prices, and browse the market without having to travel from station to station.

Searching shows all matching listings, not just the best one, and lets you compare price, amount, distance, faction, and time until restock in one place. It can also include player-built stores in search results, giving you a much better view of the wider economy and making trading with other players far more practical.
Store Block Improvements

Store Blocks have also received several important improvements. Players can now trade Hydrogen, Oxygen, and modded gases between each other through player-built Store Blocks, opening up new opportunities for player-to-player logistics, refueling services, and trade networks.

The maximum number of listings per Store Block has also been increased from 30 to 50. In addition, NPC station prices have been rebalanced so player-built stores can more easily compete in multiplayer worlds.
Economy ModAPI
Economy 2 Update also greatly expands modding support for the economy system, opening new possibilities for modders, server gamemasters, and scenario makers.

With more features exposed through the ModAPI and more SBC files open for editing, creators can build player-made contracts and contract variants, rebalance and reshape trade, and create more dynamic economies around factions, stations, and player-driven markets. It also opens up more advanced control for custom worlds and scenarios, including planet subtype blacklists for trade station and contract spawns, along with a Regenerate Station Locations admin option for scenario makers and server operators.

Contracts in Economy 2 Update have been significantly expanded and rebalanced to make them feel more rewarding, more varied, and more enjoyable to play. This update adds several new contract types, improves payouts and contract flow, and gives players more reasons to engage with stations as part of their regular gameplay loop instead of treating contracts as a simple credit grind.
Escort Contracts have also been removed, with their role now replaced by more interesting and engaging alternatives.
Courier Contracts

Courier Contracts focus on delivering packages between stations, but they are no longer just simple point-to-point jobs. They now come with different risk levels, with more dangerous deliveries offering better rewards and the possibility of pirate interference along the way.
Search Contracts

Search Contracts send you out to locate missing grids and return them to their owners. Once you find the target, the contract updates to guide you back to the delivery location, and your reward depends on the condition of the grid you bring home - giving you a good reason to recover it intact.
PvE Bounty Contracts

PvE Bounty Contracts add a new combat-focused mission type built around hunting down enemy NPC grids. These contracts give players a more direct way to take on hostile targets for rewards, and help fill the role of more action-oriented station jobs.
Hauling Contracts

Hauling Contracts task you with transporting heavy cargo containers between stations. These jobs place more emphasis on the kind of ship you bring, with container size, value, and risk affecting the reward. Damage, destruction, or tampering with the cargo can reduce your payout or fail the contract entirely, making hauling feel more like a true logistics job.
Salvage Contracts

Salvage Contracts send you to damaged or abandoned grids in search of valuable mission items. You are free to tear into the wreck, recover what you can, and keep the salvage - but the contract itself is completed by finding the target item and returning it to the station. This creates a nice mix of exploration, scavenging, and profit.
Item Recovery Contracts

Item Recovery Contracts come from exploring existing encounters in the world. Special items hidden in cargo ships, random encounters, and other points of interest can be delivered to an interested station for payment and increased reputation.
Grid Recovery Contracts

Grid Recovery Contracts give you the chance to recover damaged or derelict grids you discover while exploring and return them to their home station for a reward. These contracts help connect exploration, encounters, and the economy system more naturally, giving players another reason to venture out into the void.
This release is also a major update to faction gameplay, making NPC factions easier to discover and more interesting to interact with. Trade stations now feel more alive.

Finding new stations and factions is now much more intuitive. Trade stations can display dynamic billboard advertisements that grant GPS locations when interacted with, datapads with station locations can now appear as loot, and some encounters can trigger contracts that guide you to new stations. Any reputation change now also makes that NPC faction visible to the player, helping the world feel more connected and easier to navigate.

Reputation has also been reworked to be more flexible and easier to recover from. A hostile reputation with an NPC faction no longer blocks access to their stores or contracts - instead, those factions will offer fewer contract types and worse prices until you improve your standing. Negative reputation no longer spreads to allied factions, and reputation is no longer lost or gained from interactions between player factions.

A new world option, Reputation Decay Over Time, slowly moves reputation back toward its default values during active play, giving players a reason for continued interaction with the contract system.. This helps keep faction relationships dynamic over time instead of locking them in permanently.

This release also gives Trade Stations a major refresh with 17 new prefabs for planetary, orbital, and deep space locations. These new stations are designed to feel more varied, intuitive to navigate, and more connected to the wider world, with a broader range of station types spread across different environments.

Trade Stations now also have unique names, helping each location and playthrough feel more distinct and memorable. This includes Meridius Station, added in honor of the creator of Modular Encounters Systems. Stations can now also be discovered in more natural ways through billboard advertisements that grant GPS locations, datapads found in loot, and encounter contracts that can guide you to new locations.

Space Pirate stations have also been expanded to better reflect their faction. Different faction types can now use their own station prefabs, helping Trade Stations feel more varied depending on whether you are visiting traders, miners, builders, military factions, or pirates.

All Trade Stations now sell Hydrogen, making them more useful as reliable refueling stops during longer journeys. Together with the new station layouts, improved ship sales, and better ways to discover new locations, this update makes stations feel much more like a connected part of everyday gameplay.
Ship Prefabs / Station Sales

The ship market has also been greatly expanded with 43 new and updated purchasable grids, including ships, rovers, drones, and missiles. This gives players a much wider range of ready-made options at Trade Stations, whether you want to jump straight into combat, pick up a useful utility vehicle, or buy a solid starting point for your next custom build.

These purchasable grids are meant to be practical foundations that players can easily adapt and make their own. Many are designed to support customization and expansion, giving you a better launching point for cargo hauling, combat, exploration, or logistics without needing to start completely from scratch. Drones, rovers and even missiles are now also part of station sales, giving players even more ready-to-use options straight from the market.
Trade Stations now feel more alive thanks to the addition of animated NPC characters that move through Trade Stations, emote and react to player presence.

This feature is the result of a lot of research and experimentation on character pathfinding on custom grids, and AI reactions to player presence. We were quite successful, and this is the first stage of that work that we are ready to release and share with you.

We are adding a new free set of Structural Blocks for large grids which includes several platforms, beams, and frames. These are perfect building foundations for stations, large hangars, and support structures. These blocks expand your building palette with heavier structural pieces that feel practical, versatile, and easy to build with.
[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
Structural Blocks (7 block, L grid) - Structural Platform, Structural Platform Connector, Structural Platform Corner, Structural Frame, Diagonal Beam 3x3, Diagonal Beam 4x4, Diagonal Beam 5x5

Safe Zones have also received a set of practical quality-of-life improvements. They now automatically pull inventory like other blocks, have reduced power requirements, and no longer use a separate filter for floating objects. Floating objects can now pass through Safe Zones and come to rest much faster inside them.

We’re making great progress on the 1.209 update, adding lots of new content and features to the economy system, while simultaneously improving and expanding older elements. Over the past few weeks, contracts have been a major focus.

Many of the existing contract types are being refined to address pain points and improve their overall experience, while several brand-new contracts are being added into the mix. Our goal is to deliver an updated experience that features modernized NPC grids, dynamic situations, and objectives that encourage the use of specialized craft to get the job done.

Recovery Contracts: You never know what you might find in the void of space. The existing NPC and encounter systems now have a chance of becoming the starting point of your next big payday. Explore, discover, profit.

PvE Bounty Contracts: Jump right into the action - facing off against pirates, mercenaries, and hostiles who threaten your allies. Defeat them, keep the trade lanes secure, and earn credits for your prowess.
Hauling Contracts: Containers packed with vital supplies are ready to move. Can your ship handle the additional weight and still make the delivery window?

Salvage Contracts: Valuable items have been lost in the aftermath of a disastrous event. Track them down, return them to their rightful owner, and you’ll be generously rewarded. The client only cares about their treasures, anything else you manage to extract is yours to keep.
Whatever your playstyle is, 1.209 is sure to breathe new life into your Space Engineers experience. We can’t wait to get it into your hands!

Whether it's a vibrant high-tech space station located among an asteroid cluster, a classic sci-fi themed space cafe, or just a cool looking spaceship bristling with Ion thrusters and neon armor - we hope all of this will add to your story in a world of high technology.
This update contains much requested Hinge Blocks, Small Grid Doors, new automated Weather System, 3D Letter Blocks and more!

Hello, Engineers!
Here we go with the first major update of 2020 - we hope you’ll enjoy it!

We added Small Hydrogen Tank and a handcrafted planet Triton, which features a breathtaking snowy and frozen landscape, that players can explore and build across. We are very fortunate to have such a creative and driven modding community. We recently had the opportunity to work closely with a member of that community, the incredibly talented Jakaria. The result is Scripted Weather, which you can experience now, in the new Frostbite scenario!
Visual Scripting Tool has been reworked, allowing our players to create their own campaigns, stories and more complex experience than it is possible with modding and programmable blocks.
We also added full support for Gamepad, changed UI visuals, done more Simulation and Render optimizations and much more!
Frostbite Pack DLC is available to purchase, containing the co-op multiplayer Frostbite Scenario, Antenna Dish, 6 Dead Engineers, Gate, Offset Door, Frozen Armor Skin and 7 LCD Posters.

items.text: Hello, Engineers!

The last couple of months were busy in Keen. We were working on another major update, which we are releasing today. Hello, Engineers!

It’s time for another exciting update for Space Engineers. The most obvious change is the fact that with this release we are bringing both free and premium content to the game. This gives you the opportunity to enjoy new things, but also the chance to support the further development of Space Engineers, if you are willing to do so.

All players will get new functional cockpit LCDs with customizable screens, replay tool, which can be used for setting up various animated scenes, brand new random Encounters, Steam trading cards, badges and backgrounds, and all bug fixes, optimizations, and smaller improvements for free.
Players who already own the Deluxe Edition will also get three new music tracks based on the music from our trailers.

For players who wish to support further development of Space Engineers, we have created a bulk of Decorative Blocks, which you can use for various decorations on your spaceships, vehicles and space stations. The price is $3.99 USD, or your regional Steam equivalent. You can purchase the Decorative Pack here:

If you decide not to purchase the Decorative Pack, but you want to play with friends or other players who did buy the Decorative Pack, you will still be able to join a multiplayer game or server with them and enjoy the game. In this case, you will be able to view these new blocks, but you won’t be able to build or interact with them.
Marek's blog post: https://blog.marekrosa.org/2019/04/space-engineers-customizable-lcd.html
Full list of features and improvements: https://forum.keenswh.com/threads/7402960
FAQ
Q: Are all future updates going to be paid?

A: Actually, even this update isn’t paid. The major part of this update (LCD screens, Replay Tool, new music tracks, smaller improvements) is free for everyone. Only the smaller and not mandatory part is paid - Decorative Pack.
Q: Aren’t you going to split the community - people who don’t own the Decorative Pack won’t be able to play with people who own it?

A: The way we designed this is that even people who don’t purchase the Decorative Pack can play on servers with people who own the Decorative Pack. Players who don’t own the Decorative Pack won’t be able to build with these new blocks, nor interact with them, but they will be able to view them in-game.
Q: Where is all this money going?

A: To support future development of Space Engineers and other leading-edge projects we plan to work on at Keen Software House. Players kept asking us for something they could buy to support the development of Space Engineers, and the Decorative Pack is a great option for them.
Q: When did you start working on Decorative Pack?
A: Right after Space Engineers left early access and all hot issues were resolved. Most of the work was done by the Art team, the rest of the developers is working on other long-term updates.
Q: Why haven’t you increased the price of Space Engineers and include the Decorative Pack in it, or why it’s not part of the Deluxe Edition?

A: We want more people to play Space Engineers, which means we must lower the barrier of entry. When the Space Engineers community grows, everyone benefits from this - more content on Workshop, more mods, more new ideas, more people to play with. This means that all non-mandatory features should be optional, so only those who really want them can pay for them. That’s why we decreased the price of Space Engineers, and made the Decorative Pack an optional purchase.
Q: We asked you for volumetric water, compound blocks, new goals, more optimizations, etc, and instead you are giving us a toilet block?

A: Hehe, if you put it this way, it sounds kind of funny. :) But the reality is that decorative blocks are low-hanging fruit, not a bottleneck towards those other mentioned future features. Additionally, the decorative pack can bring added profit and make the mentioned things happen.
Hello, Engineers!

February 28, 2019 is the day for all Space Engineers. Today, we are moving Space Engineers out of Early Access. Getting Space Engineers out of Early Access has been planned for a long time. We have worked on it basically since 2016/2017, when the game entered beta. It was our goal to release the game in the state we consider to fulfill our original vision, including all planned features and core game components. Moreover, the game includes a lot of things that were not planned at the beginning of development (solar panels, planets, rotors, pistons, wheels, and many more features).
Space Engineers was one of the first Early Access games on Steam and one of the few titles to be successfully released after several years of passionate development. We keep our promises!

Space Engineers has been in Early Access for 5+ years, and during this period we developed the game from a proof-of-concept to a feature complete space engineering sandbox. We sold more than 3 million copies and we have more than 200,000 monthly active players.

Because Space Engineers development was open, you were able to see what’s happening under the hood. Contrary to other products, where you see the final product, but don’t see how the project has been developed and changed over time, and what challenges the development team had to overcome.

With this update, we are also setting a new price for Space Engineers to $19.99. According to our analysis and tests, this price better suits the majority of Space Engineers fans. This change also brings all regional prices on Steam to match countries specifications and regional differences.
Marek's blog post: https://blog.marekrosa.org/2019/02/space-engineers-released.html

Hello, Engineers!

After six months, we are releasing the next major update, which is focusing on the complete overhaul of multiplayer in Space Engineers, and a number of new features and optimizations. This was a massive overhaul and that’s why it wasn’t possible to make this update in weekly increment - so thanks a lot for your patience!

We had to redo major parts of the engine and there was a lot of experimentation - for example changing the prediction protocol on client-server and observing if it’s better for user experience or worse, and many more. Space Engineers has many systems and special care had to be taken for each of them: player character, jetpack, ship, wheeled vehicles, voxels and planets, fast moving objects, deformable entities, antennas, player standing on a moving grid, colliding grids, rotors, pistons, wheels, and many many more.
But wait - that's not all! With this massive multiplayer update we are releasing optimizations and performance improvements, Safe Zones, Female Engineer and much more!
